newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb damages council building in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Bomb damages council building in Corsica.

text.p: A bomb damaged a local authority building in Corsica late on Monday but no one was injured, paramilitary gendarmes said on Tuesday.
The building in Biguglia, which houses technical services of the regional council of northern Corsica, had already been damaged earlier this month by a blast which destroyed several nearby offices.
The head of the regional council, Paul Natali, has received death threats from "Fronte Ribellu", a breakaway wing of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC).
Villas, offices or work sites of the Natali family have been bombed seven times in the past two years.
Hardline FLNC guerrillas said on Monday that they had carried out three attacks on the French Mediterranean island in the past 10 days.

The FLNC stepped up its two-decade-old guerrilla campaign for greater autonomy for Corsica after Francois Santoni, head of its legal wing, the Conculta Naziunalista, was detained on December 16 on suspicion of attempted extortion and arms violations.
